The SLS is in Villigen in the canton of Aargau and has been in operation since 2001. Its storage ring has a circumference of 288 metres and lies in a round building. Along about 20 **beamlines**, the light is led to experiment stations. In **top-up operation**, the ring is constantly refilled with small amounts of electrons so that the current, and therefore the brightness, stays the same.

An important area of use is **protein crystallography**. This is used to find out exactly how proteins made of millions of atoms are built. Pharmaceutical companies use this knowledge to develop suitable medicines. At the SLS, batteries, rocks, materials or even old works of art are also examined with X-rays without damaging them.

From 2023 to 2025 the storage ring was completely renewed in the **SLS 2.0** project. New magnets bundle the electron beam much more tightly. According to the PSI, the **emittance**, the measure of how well the beam is bundled, improves by up to a factor of 40. This makes the X-ray light even brighter and sharper, and experiments become faster and more precise.

The **Paul Scherrer Institute** is the largest research institute for natural sciences and engineering in Switzerland. Besides the SLS, it runs other large facilities, such as the SwissFEL X-ray laser and a neutron source. Every year, researchers from many countries come to Villigen to carry out measurements at these facilities. The PSI lies on the River Aare and is part of the ETH Domain.

begriffe.erklaerung: A ring-shaped tunnel in which electrons fly round in a circle for a long time.
Very bright light that electrons give off on curved paths.
A measure of how tightly the electron beam is bundled.
An important building block of all living things.

gewusst: The electrons in the SLS circle the 288-metre ring about a million times per second.
Synchrotron light was first discovered as an annoying side effect of particle accelerators, before special facilities were built for it.

teile.einleitung: Algorithmic bias means that a computer program treats certain groups of people unfairly. This often happens because the data from which an artificial intelligence learns contains prejudices or gaps. Because such programs make more and more decisions, the topic is very important.
wichtigste: Algorithmic bias often comes from one-sided or incomplete training data.
In 2018 the “Gender Shades” study showed that facial analysis made the most mistakes with women with dark skin.
Around 2018 Amazon stopped using an AI system for selecting job applications because it disadvantaged women.
In 2016 ProPublica criticised the COMPAS software because of different error rates.
A seemingly neutral feature that is closely linked to a protected feature is called a proxy variable.
Checking the error rates separately for different groups of people helps to uncover bias.
The EU’s AI Act sets strict requirements for risky AI systems, for example for decisions about staff.

abschnitte.text: An **algorithm** is an exact set of instructions that a computer follows. Many modern programs learn their rules themselves from large amounts of data. If this data is one-sided, the program takes on the one-sidedness. This is then called **algorithmic bias**. The program seems neutral, but it makes systematically unfair decisions.

abschnitte.titel: Where does the problem come from?
abschnitte.text: Often certain groups are missing from the **training data**, or they appear much less often. Sometimes the data also reflects old injustices. A language model may, for example, link “pilot” more with men and “nurse” more with women, because it takes on frequencies from human texts. Even seemingly neutral details such as where someone lives can act as a **proxy variable**. They are closely linked with features for which nobody may be disadvantaged.

In 2018 the researcher **Joy Buolamwini** examined commercial facial analysis in the “Gender Shades” study. The error rate was highest for women with dark skin and lowest for men with light skin. Around 2018 Amazon stopped using an experimental system for selecting job applications, because it rated applications from women lower. In 2016 the journalism organisation ProPublica criticised the **COMPAS** software, which was meant to predict in the USA whether offenders would reoffend.

Some errors reinforce themselves. In predictive policing, a program sends more patrols to a particular neighbourhood. More incidents are then discovered there, which produces new data. This data in turn triggers more patrols. In this way a **feedback loop** develops, even if no more happens in the neighbourhood than anywhere else.

The most direct help is to check the **error rates** separately for different groups of people. Varied training data and teams who look at a system from different points of view are also important. With the **AI Act**, the EU has created rules that sort AI systems according to their risk. Systems for decisions about staff are regarded there as particularly risky. In Switzerland too, people are discussing how AI can be used fairly and safely.

begriffe.erklaerung: An exact step-by-step set of instructions that a computer follows.
The examples from which an artificial intelligence learns.
A seemingly neutral feature that is closely linked to a protected feature.
The share of cases in which a program gets it wrong.
When people are treated unfairly because of a feature.

gewusst: Joy Buolamwini noticed the problem because a face recognition system only recognised her face when she wore a white mask.
A program can be unfair even though nobody programmed it that way on purpose.
Simply leaving out a feature such as gender is often not enough, because other data can give it away.
